value.title: PR 133 s12 answered and notification admission review

sections.name: body
sections.value:
PR 133 s12 is blocked at 9919d4d9e5752ac9e5f942be268d61283daa0e04 with two source-proven P2s. Scope is the plan 205 time-limit delta on reviewed PR 129 base 314da13; the pending P001/index merge needs a later exact-head delta check.

F001: the indexed query excludes answered_at rows only when the round takes its snapshot. The round then awaits the latest holder card. Both notification stamp UPDATEs check only their own NULL column, so an answer committed during that await does not prevent a later check-in or escalation. Notification admission must atomically lose to an already-committed answer. Add a deterministic card-read barrier case for both stages.

F002: checkin_at/escalated_at are committed before target resolution and audit/delivery admission. Missing targets, failed audit/admission or a process interruption consumes the action; escalated_at also permanently removes the request from the open partial index. Record retryable intent and durable handoff, not a terminal sent timestamp for an attempt. Stable message ids plus a recoverable outbox/claim preserve idempotency without losing notices.

The ordinary two-window timing, ongoing pre-check-in card updates and C5 default/explicit/unlimited cases pass. Exact-head CI run 42176950725 and junit-linux artifact 13484055607 contain all three s12 testcase receipts; 1971 tests passed, five skipped globally, all four jobs green. ddocs CI explicitly UNAVAILABLE. No local builds, tests, runtime probes or mutation checks were run under CI-first policy.

Verdict: roles/reviewer/outputs/2026-11/pr-133-verdict.md. Security owns escalation recipients/audit, performance owns per-round scaling. The harness improvement is answer-versus-admission and failure/restart notification fixtures, not additional successful stamp-once assertions.
